chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Ross Russell, Dial Records and 'Moose The Mooche'
summary: Ross Russell's Tempo store leads to Parker's first Dial date; Parker sings 'Moose The Mooche' for Moose the paraplegic fan.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: During this period, I had moved over to Howard's; I was living with Howard. And Ross Russell from Dial Records had a record shop up on Hollywood Boulevard called Tempo Music, Tempo Records, rather. He was at Howard's house one Sunday having dinner with us, and he said, 'Well, I'm thinking about making a record on this guy, Charlie Parker.' So we said, 'Yeah! Why not!' So that was the beginning of Dial Records, when he made the first date on Charlie Parker.

In fact, I remember before they made that date, Charlie had just written 'Moose The Mooche,' and he came over and he sang it to me, sang the melody to 'Moose The Mooche.' I imagine you've heard of the legendary Moose. He was a paraplegic and a real Jazz lover. And he used to sit at the corner of the bar at the Downbeat Club -- that was his stationary place. And everybody knew Moose. So he named this song for Moose -- 'Moose The Mooche.' And he also sang 'Yardbird Suite.'
We were all close. Because he used to come and hang out over at Howard's place during the daytime, and we would
listen to records... Because Howard had a vast library of records, Classical records and Jazz records, and all ..(?).. all the good things he had. Because he had them shipped out here from...
